---
title: "Cell2Cell | Data cleaning and shared split"
output:
  html_document:
    code_folding: hide
---

We used the supplied Cell2Cell CSV, a cross-sectional record of customer usage,
billing, service, equipment, and retention history. The file contains 51,047
customers and 58 fields, including 14,711 recorded churners (28.8%). The case
dictionary describes approximately 71,000 customers. The supplied file defines
the analysis sample. The binary churn outcome has no verified prediction
horizon, so its sample rate cannot be read as monthly churn.

The business question is which customers to review first when the retention
team has limited outreach capacity. Cleaning keeps the recorded values and
their units traceable across model comparisons.

The churn label describes the recorded observation period. In the raw CSV,
`Yes` means the customer left and `No` means they stayed during that period.

## Data preparation

```{r audit}
customers <- read.csv(
  "Provided_Data/cell2celltrain.csv",
  na.strings = c("", "NA"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stopifnot(!anyNA(customers$CustomerID),
          anyDuplicated(customers$CustomerID) == 0L,
          !anyNA(customers$Churn),
          setequal(unique(customers$Churn), c("No", "Yes")))

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Customers = nrow(customers),
    Fields = ncol(customers),
    `Duplicate rows` = sum(duplicated(customers)),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  caption = "Source file at a glance",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
churn_label <- factor(customers$Churn, levels = c("No", "Yes"),
                      labels = c("Did not churn", "Churned"))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(churn_label)),
             col.names = c("Observed churn outcome", "Customers"),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

missing <- sort(colSums(is.na(customers)), decreasing = TRUE)
```

### Imported fields and missing counts

```{r imported-fields}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  field = names(missing),
  imported_type = vapply(customers[names(missing)], class, character(1)),
  missing = unname(missing),
  row.names = NULL
), col.names = c("Field", "Imported type", "Missing cells"))
```

```{r source-flags}
source_flags <- c(
  unknown_handset_price = sum(customers$HandsetPrice == "Unknown", na.rm = TRUE),
  zero_age_hh1 = sum(customers$AgeHH1 == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  zero_age_hh2 = sum(customers$AgeHH2 == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  negative_equipment_days = sum(customers$CurrentEquipmentDays < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  negative_monthly_revenue = sum(customers$MonthlyRevenue < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Check = c("Unknown handset prices", "Zero primary household ages",
              "Zero secondary household ages", "Negative equipment days",
              "Negative monthly revenue"),
    Customers = unname(source_flags)
  ),
  caption = "Source values flagged for review",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

### Cleaning rules

| Item | What happened in the shared dataset | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Blank fields and literal `NA` tokens | Set to R's `NA` when reading the source CSV through `na.strings = c("", "NA")`. | They represent unavailable values. |
| `HandsetPrice` | Set all 28,982 cells containing the literal text `Unknown` to R's `NA`, then converted the column to numeric USD. The resulting missing prices are numeric `NA` values. | Recorded prices can now be summarized and modeled as amounts. |
| `CurrentEquipmentDays` | Replaced negative values with `NA`. | Elapsed time with a handset must be zero or positive. |
| Zero household ages | Flagged for review and kept as recorded. | The meaning of zero is unverified, and age is outside the current predictor sets. |
| Negative monthly revenue | Flagged for review and kept in USD. | Signed amounts may reflect billing adjustments. |
| Scaling and clipping | Kept original units. No z-score standardization, min–max normalization, or outlier clipping was applied. | The current unpenalized logistic models can fit predictors in different units. Original units make revenue, tenure, and usage easier to interpret. |
| Customer records | Checked that customer IDs were unique and that every row had a valid churn label. Kept all rows. | Records with missing predictors can still contribute valid data. |

```{r clean}
prepared <- customers
price <- prepared$HandsetPrice
price[which(price == "Unknown")] <- NA
prepared$HandsetPrice <- as.numeric(price)
stopifnot(all(is.na(price) == is.na(prepared$HandsetPrice)))

invalid_equipment <- which(prepared$CurrentEquipmentDays < 0)
prepared$CurrentEquipmentDays[invalid_equipment] <- NA
missing_after_cleaning <- sort(colSums(is.na(prepared)), decreasing = TRUE)
```

### Cleaned fields and missing counts

```{r cleaned-fields}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  field = names(missing_after_cleaning),
  cleaned_type = vapply(prepared[names(missing_after_cleaning)], class, character(1)),
  missing_after_cleaning = unname(missing_after_cleaning),
  row.names = NULL
), col.names = c("Field", "Cleaned type", "Missing cells"))
```

### Before and after cleaning

The field-level table counts missing cells. The customer-level table counts
each customer once if any field is missing.

```{r cleaning-impact}
source_tokens <- read.csv("Provided_Data/cell2celltrain.csv",
                          colClasses = "character", na.strings = NULL)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  source_encoding = c("Empty field", "Literal NA"),
  imported_as_na = c(sum(source_tokens == "", na.rm = TRUE),
                     sum(source_tokens == "NA", na.rm = TRUE))
))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  field = c("HandsetPrice", "CurrentEquipmentDays"),
  newly_marked_missing = c(sum(customers$HandsetPrice == "Unknown", na.rm = TRUE),
                           length(invalid_equipment)),
  missing_before = unname(missing[c("HandsetPrice", "CurrentEquipmentDays")]),
  missing_after = unname(missing_after_cleaning[c("HandsetPrice", "CurrentEquipmentDays")])
))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  measure = c("Customer rows", "Cells marked missing", "Rows with any missing field"),
  before = c(nrow(customers), sum(missing), sum(!complete.cases(customers))),
  after = c(nrow(prepared), sum(missing_after_cleaning), sum(!complete.cases(prepared)))
))
```

### What this means

Before cleaning, `HandsetPrice` had **0 cells counted as missing** because
the source encoded 28,982 unavailable prices as the literal text `Unknown`.
R counted that text as a recorded value. After replacing each `Unknown` with
R's `NA`, the missing-price count rose to **28,982**. Those prices were
already unavailable in the source data. Cleaning made that explicit.

For `CurrentEquipmentDays`, the missing count rose from **1 to 77** because
76 negative values were replaced with `NA`. Together, these two changes
account for the increase from **3,515 to 32,573** cells counted as missing.

### Where missing values are filled

R stores missing values as `NA`. The export uses `write.csv(..., na = "")`,
so those cells appear as empty fields in the shared CSV. EDA reports missingness
where applicable. In `03_Variable_Selection.Rmd`, each cross-validation fit
fills missing numeric predictors with the median of observed values in that
fold's fitting rows. For example, a missing handset price in a validation row
gets the median recorded price from the fitting rows. Missing categorical
predictors use the most frequent category in the fitting rows. These temporary
replacements apply to both fitting and validation data and stay inside the
modeling step. This prevents validation data from influencing imputation.

### Field consistency checks

```{r consistency}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  check = c("Active lines exceed unique lines", "Zero usage with positive dropped calls",
            "Combined network count differs from sum by more than 0.1"),
  flagged = with(prepared, c(
    sum(ActiveSubs > UniqueSubs, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(MonthlyMinutes == 0 & DroppedCalls > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(abs(DroppedBlockedCalls - DroppedCalls - BlockedCalls) > 0.1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )),
  comparable = with(prepared, c(
    sum(complete.cases(ActiveSubs, UniqueSubs)),
    sum(complete.cases(MonthlyMinutes, DroppedCalls)),
    sum(complete.cases(DroppedBlockedCalls, DroppedCalls, BlockedCalls))
  ))
))
```

### What this means

These checks flag where engineered features need guards or where measurement
windows need confirmation. The original source fields remain available.
There are 12 records with zero monthly minutes and positive dropped calls.
The combined network count differs from the sum of the two component
counts by more than 0.1 in 5,695 records. We compare it as an alternate
predictor and keep the source measurements available for review.
The case dictionary identifies zero secondary household age as possible for
single-person households. Training-only missingness comparisons appear in
`02_EDA.Rmd`.

### Seasonality and calendar dates

The case dictionary describes one cross-sectional record per customer. The
CSV has no observation date, billing period, or churn event date. The
quarter-over-quarter change fields show the direction and size of a change
but do not identify calendar quarters. `MonthsInService` measures elapsed
tenure. A change by tenure cannot be assigned to November or Black Friday.
Testing seasonality would require dated customer billing or usage records
spanning multiple periods. Daily or weekly dates would be needed to isolate
Black Friday from the rest of November.

## Shared training, test, and cross-validation assignments

We use a 75/25 split stratified by churn and three stratified CV folds
within training, with seed 445 for each assignment. This preserves the
assignments used in the preliminary analysis. The test partition has a blank
CV fold. For fold 1, the model fits on folds 2 and 3 and scores fold 1. Each
training fold serves as validation once. The test partition is reserved
for final evaluation after the team locks the model and predictors.

```{r split-and-export}
set.seed(445)
by_churn <- split(seq_len(nrow(prepared)), prepared$Churn)
train_rows <- unlist(lapply(by_churn, function(rows) {
  sample(rows, floor(0.75 * length(rows)))
}), use.names = FALSE)
test_rows <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(prepared)), train_rows)
manifest_rows <- c(train_rows, test_rows)
manifest <- data.frame(
  CustomerID = prepared$CustomerID[manifest_rows],
  split = rep(c("train", "test"), c(length(train_rows), length(test_rows))),
  cv_fold = NA_integer_
)

set.seed(445)
train_by_churn <- split(seq_along(train_rows), prepared$Churn[train_rows])
for (rows in train_by_churn) {
  manifest$cv_fold[rows] <- sample(rep(1:3, length.out = length(rows)))
}

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(manifest$CustomerID),
          setequal(prepared$CustomerID, manifest$CustomerID),
          all(manifest$cv_fold[manifest$split == "train"] %in% 1:3),
          all(is.na(manifest$cv_fold[manifest$split == "test"])))
split_labels <- factor(manifest$split, levels = c("train", "test"),
                       labels = c("Training", "Reserved test"))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(split_labels, churn_label[manifest_rows])),
             caption = "Customer counts by partition and observed churn outcome",
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(manifest$cv_fold, churn_label[manifest_rows])),
             caption = "Customer counts within each training fold",
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

dir.create("Generated_Data", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(prepared, "Generated_Data/cleaned_data.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(manifest, "Generated_Data/split_manifest.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

The cleaned master retains all source columns for auditing and exploration.
Use `CustomerID` to join the two files and use the eligibility review in
`02_EDA.Rmd` before choosing predictors.
